Folklore Presence. When you first encounter an NPC group, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met as omen, trophy, or legend. It is never neutral. People have heard of your kind. They are almost always wrong, and that is almost always useful.

A wax-paper sandwich that re-folds itself when you set it down. Take a bite, set it down, look up, look back: re-wrapped. Take another bite, set it down. Re-wrapped. The bread stays fresh. description.value:
"I see what you actually are."

Refraction: Truth — perception bent toward exposure; lies, concealment, the thing that does not want to be named.

The Refraction of Truth makes hiding impossible. Your Surge spends strip cover: read a foe true so its defenses fail, name the lie so it stops working, and lay an enemy so bare it has nowhere left to put a single intention.

Refraction (spent via Surge)

  • The Reading Eye (1) — a foe rolls its saves rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2 (you read it true).
  • The Unconcealed Word (2) — a foe is Staggered and its next attack is rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2.
  • The Exposure (5) — a foe cannot take reactions and rolls its saves rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2.

"Every structure has a flaw. You only have to look at it correctly."

The Wyrdlens Adept turns perception into force. You run on Surge like everyone, and yours arrives when you land a manifestation (bank +1, max +2/round) — every revelation feeds the lens. The free Probability Overlay (1/round reroll-lowest, refreshes at the start of your turn) stays as your innate edge.

The Lens (spent via Surge)

  • Foresight (1) — you or an ally banks a reroll-lowest (you saw the thread).
  • Expose (2) — a foe's next attack and its saves are rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2 (you read the seam).
  • Refract (3) — an ally gains DR equal to Tier and a freed reaction (harm bends aside).
  • Revelation (5) — allies within 6 squares bank a reroll; a foe's next attack is rolling 3d10 and keeping the lowest 2.

Tikkun Sight endures — once per Soma Break, treat a misfire as a base-tier success (the Tree pays in Clarity instead).

Cryptidkin Subspecies. This heritage preserves the original UUID for Furrykin while converting it from a species-root with five sub-clades into a single flexible Cryptidkin subspecies.

“You are not an animal that learned to talk. You are a person the world made with fur because it needed you to survive.”

Furrykin. You are anything fur-bearing the world decided to make people out of. Talking badger, cunning fox, stoic bear, watchful rabbit, the uncle-shaped thing the trappers call Bigfoot—all valid. Size and frame are flexible; the instinct is not.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium (choose at creation; Medium Furrykin can describe themselves as “large and shaggy” without mechanical change—Bigfoot-scale creatures still move and fight at Medium).

  • Speed. 6 squares

  • Subspecies Lean. No fixed stat lean. Your frame is your business—the Tier powers adapt to how you play it.

Core: Folklore & Frame

At creation you gain Folklore & Frame (Folklore Presence, Wasteland Adapted, Survivor’s Instinct).

Wildframe & Instinct (Furrykin Extras)

  • Wildframe. Your body is built for a world that bites back. You already reroll the lowest die on checks against disease and environmental poison (from Wasteland Adapted); as Furrykin, you also add your tier to any Body defense check to resist Stress.

  • Keen Sense. Choose one: Keen Smell, Keen Hearing, or Keen Sight. You reroll the lowest die on Perception checks relying on that sense.

  • Frame Choice. Choose one narrative frame at creation: Predator (bite or claws count as unarmed strikes that deal 1d6 instead of 1d4), Forager (trained in Athletics), or Brute (count as one size larger for carrying, shoving, and grappling).

Furrykin Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17). Tier powers previously split across Felid / Leporid / Mustelid / Ursid / Vulpin are unified; choose flavor at the table without mechanical separation.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Exorcist / Purifier.

“You don’t negotiate with the darkness. You end it.”

Exorcists do not bargain. They do not reinterpret. They do not accept corruption as a usable state.

To an Exorcist, the Great Work is not about managing the broken world. It is about removing what should not be there and restoring the conditions under which something honest can exist again.

Where Goetics bind, Exorcists sever. Where Shamans listen, Exorcists intervene. Where Kabbalists align, Exorcists cleanse.

How Exorcists pursue the Great Work:

  • By removing Qliphothic influence and corruption
  • By stabilizing Hexes under Darkness pressure
  • By preventing the spread of systemic decay
  • By refusing to let harmful systems persist just because they are useful

Resonance: Tiferet / Purity — clarity, balance, and the reassertion of what should be.

Tell-tales: still air where there should be movement, silence after tension, things that stop being wrong without explanation.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 specialty edge on actions involving stabilization, cleansing, or anti-corruption pressure

Cost Principle: removal is violent in its own way. Expect rigidity, collateral suppression, and consequences when something removed turns out to have been holding something worse in place.
